name: CZECHIA

flag.title: Flag of Czechia
flag.note: White, red & blue with blue wedge at hoist

lead: Czechia is in the middle of Europe. Germany, Austria, Slovakia and Poland surround it, so it has no sea. It has fairy-tale castles and golden beer. Prague is one of Earth's best-kept medieval cities.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Pop. 1.4 m — city on the Vltava

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Gentle mountains ring the country. The west has rolling Bohemian hills. The east has Moravia's flat plains, with vineyards and folk festivals.
The Vltava River winds 430 km through Czechia, under Prague's famous bridges. Then it joins the Elbe. Pine forests cover the Šumava mountains. Wolves, lynx and otters live there.
animals: The Eurasian lynx is a spotted wildcat the size of a labrador. Hunters wiped it out. People brought it back to the Šumava forest in the 1980s. Around 60 now live in the Bohemian hills.
Red deer bellow in misty autumn valleys. White-tailed eagles soar over South Bohemia's fishponds. The great bustard, Europe's heaviest flying bird, still strolls across Moravian fields.
culture: Czechs drink more beer per person than anyone on Earth, about 150 litres a year. Pilsen invented pale lager in 1842. The Pilsner Urquell brewery still makes it there.
Marionettes (string puppets) are an old Czech art. Wooden puppets perform whole operas. Every Christmas Eve, families watch fairy-tale films together.
history: Bohemia was the heart of the Holy Roman Empire under Charles IV. He founded Central Europe's first university in 1348. He also built Charles Bridge in 1357.

In 1968, Soviet tanks crushed the Prague Spring reforms. In 1989, students filled Wenceslas Square. After 43 days of peaceful protest, communist rule ended without a shot. This was the Velvet Revolution.
wows: Czechia has over 2,000 castles and châteaux.
Prague Castle is the world's largest ancient castle complex, at nearly 70,000 square metres.
Karel Čapek invented the word 'robot' in his 1920 play R.U.R.
Otto Wichterle invented soft contact lenses at home, on Christmas Day 1961.
Czechs have drunk the most beer per person every year since 1993.
Jan Jánský first fully sorted blood into ABO types in 1907.
Czechia has 16 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

myths.myth: Czech Republic and Czechoslovakia are the same
myths.fact: Czechoslovakia split peacefully on 1 January 1993. Czechia and Slovakia became two countries.
Prague is farther west than Vienna. 'Eastern Europe' was a Cold War label, not a map fact.
